## Definitions

- [passage] - A high Docs Examined : Returned Ratio means the query is scanning many documents to return few results, which can be a sign of an inefficient query or missing indexes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, index
- [passage] Query selectivity refers to how well the query predicate filters out documents in a collection. Query selectivity determines whether queries can use indexes effectively. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization/ · keywords: index, index effectiveness · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-optimization.md

For details, see [Query Shapes.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md#std-label-query-shapes) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/currentOp.md#output-fields · keywords: query shape, queryShapeHash · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/

- [passage] A query shape is a set of specifications that group similar queries together. Specifications can include filters, sorts, projections, aggregation pipeline stages, a namespace, and others. Queries that have similar specifications have the same query shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes.md

- [passage] $queryStats groups queries with common properties into the same output document. The resulting document is called a query stats entry. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] $indexStats is not allowed in transactions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats/ · keywords: $indexStats

## Structure and components

- [passage] - If `hasSort` is set to `true`, this indicates that the query contains a [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) method. Unindexed [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) methods can be very resource intensive. Check your search index configuration and confirm whether it supports the [`sort()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.sort.md#mongodb-method-cursor.sort) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, index, hasSort, true, sort()
- [passage] 2. Before creating the index, validate that no documents in the collection violate the index constraints. If a collection is distributed across shards and a shard contains a chunk with duplicate documents, the create index operation may succeed on the shards without duplicates but not on the shard with duplicates. To avoid leaving inconsistent indexes across shards, you can issue the [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) from a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) to drop the index from the collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/build-indexes-on-sharded-clusters.md#before-you-begin · keywords: $indexStats, index, db.collection.dropIndex(), mongos · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md
- [passage] The [Query Profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#std-label-query-profiler) contains several metrics you can use to pinpoint specific inefficient queries. You can visualize up to the past 24 hours of query operations. The Query Profiler can show the Examined : Returned Ratio (index keys examined to documents returned) of logged queries, which might help you identify the queries that triggered a [`Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-conditions.md#mongodb-alert-Query-Targeting--Scanned---Returned) alert. The chart shows the number of index keys examined to fulfill a query relative to the actual number of returned documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting.md#query-profiler · keywords: database profiler, index, Query Targeting: Scanned / Returned

The chart shows the number of index keys examined to fulfill a query relative to the actual number of returned documents. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: database profiler, index
- [passage] Query shapes exposing field names but redacted values may contain user PII (Personally Identifiable Information). To view truncated or full query shapes in Query Shape Insights, you must have one of the project roles listed above, which each give access to view PII (Personally Identifiable Information). For users without these permissions, Query Shape Insights identifies query shapes by their query shape hash. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#required-access · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/
- [passage] The Query Shape Insights table contains one row for each top query shape in your project, where top query shapes are determined by highest total execution time. Each row contains the query shape or its query shape hash, the namespace of the query shape, the query command, and any metrics that you select to display. You can use the Edit Columns button to choose which of the following metrics to include as table columns: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#view-metrics-in-charts-and-tables · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/

- [passage] The total number queries that performed a collection scan. The total consists of queries that did and did not use a [tailable cursor.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/tailable-cursors.md#std-label-tailable-cursors-landing-page) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/serverStatus.md#metrics · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] Field values. $queryStats normalizes field values in a query to their data types (such as number or string) when the query is recorded. $queryStats never stores field values that contain user data. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] $queryStats returns an array of query stats entries. Some query stats entry properties contain literal values, and some properties are normalized to group common queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] MongoDB 9.0 updates the $queryStats output structure to improve metrics organization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] The UTC time when $queryStats read this entry from the $queryStats virtual collection. asOf does not necessarily return the same UTC time for each result. Internally, the data structure is partitioned, and each partition will be read at an individual point in time. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] Contains aggregated runtime metrics associated with each query stats entry. Each query stats entry records statistics for each query that shares the same key. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] Contains the query shape and additional query attributes that group a set of queries together — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] Contains attributes used to group similar queries together. For more information, see Query Shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] MongoDB omits counters with a count of zero and omits subdocuments that contain no counters. If none of the recorded queries produced plan shape counters, MongoDB omits the planShapeCounters document entirely. For example, a query that matches a single document by _id uses a fast path that doesn't match any tracked plan shape, so its query stats entry contains no planShapeCounters document. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] The key.queryShape document contains query shape fields. To learn about query shapes, see Query Shapes. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] Query stats entries may contain a metrics.supplementalMetrics document that provides additional information about your queries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md

- [passage] When MongoDB logs `$queryStats` output, the results are redacted and anonymized. `$queryStats` output does not contain literals or field values. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/toggle-logging.md#about-this-task · keywords: query shape, $queryStats

- [passage] If a command with a specific query shape is rejected, MongoDB logs a message that states the query command was rejected. The message contains the query namespace, queryShapeHash, and the command with the rejected query. MongoDB only logs the message if the log verbosity level is set to at least 2. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: query shape

## How it works

- [passage] Each index suggestion includes an Average Query Targeting score indicating how many documents were read for every document returned for the index's corresponding query shapes. A score of 1 represents very efficient query shapes because every document read matched the query and was returned with the query results. All suggested indexes represent an opportunity to improve query performance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#query-targeting · keywords: index, query optimization, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [statement] Percona PMM can retain index-usage metrics across restarts when the exporter is started with -collect.indexusage (not on by default); as of the 2018 post, the metrics lacked database and collection labels, so collection-level filtering was not possible. Likely outdated. — https://www.percona.com/blog/identifying-unused-indexes-in-mongodb/ · keywords: $indexStats, index, Index Analysis with $indexStats and Unused-Index Detection
- [fact] Atlas 'Query Targeting: Scanned Objects / Returned' alerts when average documents scanned divided by average documents returned, server-wide over a sampling period, exceeds a threshold. The default threshold is 1000:1 and the docs say the ideal ratio is close to 1. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/alert-resolutions/query-targeting/ · keywords: index, index effectiveness, Index Effectiveness Measurement
- [passage] When evaluating the clauses in the [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) expression, MongoDB performs a collection scan or an index scan. If all clauses are supported by indexes, MongoDB performs index scans. To use indexes to evaluate an [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) expression, all the clauses in the [`$or`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#mongodb-query-op.-or) expression must be supported by indexes. Otherwise, MongoDB performs a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or.md#or-clauses-and-indexes · keywords: database profiler, index, $or · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/query/or/
- [passage] Recommended indexes are accompanied by sample queries, grouped by [query shape](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-query-shape), that were run against a collection that would benefit from the suggested index. The Performance Advisor considers workload activity across all nodes in the replica set, including secondaries, when generating index recommendations. The Performance Advisor doesn't negatively affect the performance of your Atlas clusters. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md · keywords: index, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/
- [passage] The index definitions laid out in the previous section illustrate one of the flexibility enhancements of `$search`. In order to create the `$text` index on `sample_mflix.movies`, you must first delete any existing text index on the sample data using the [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) method, as MongoDB supports only a single text index per collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/recommend-search-text.md#improve-flexibility-of-full-text-queries-with-mongodb-search · keywords: $indexStats, index, $search, $text, sample_mflix.movies, db.collection.dropIndex()
- [passage] The index only supports queries on fields included in the `wildcardProjection` object. In this example, MongoDB performs a collection scan for the following query because it includes a field that is not present in the `wildcardProjection` object: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/create-wildcard-index-multiple-fields.md#results · keywords: database profiler, index, wildcardProjection
- [passage] For replica sets, run [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) on the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary). The primary stops the index build and creates an associated "abortIndexBuild" [oplog](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-oplog) entry. Secondaries which replicate the "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry stop the in-progress index build and discard the build job. See [Index Build Process](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-build-process) for detailed documentation on the index build process. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#stop-in-progress-index-builds · keywords: $indexStats, index, db.collection.dropIndex() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/dropIndexes.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndexes.md
- [passage] The [`notablescan`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.notablescan) parameter does not allow unbounded queries that use a clustered index because the queries require a full collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results.md#collection-scan · keywords: database profiler, index, notablescan
- [passage] The notablescan parameter does not allow unbounded queries that use a clustered index because the queries require a full collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/explain-results/ · keywords: database profiler, index
- [fact] Each $indexStats result document carries name, key, host, accesses {ops, since}, spec, and shard (sharded clusters only); building appears only when true and spec.hidden only when true. accesses.ops counts user operations that used the index; accesses.since is when statistics gathering began. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats/ · keywords: $indexStats, index, Index Analysis with $indexStats and Unused-Index Detection
- [fact] Detection recipe: run $indexStats then filter accesses.ops equal to 0 (excluding _id_); treat as candidates only after a representative window. Netdata suggests at least 24h uptime under representative load and a full workload cycle if a restart happened after the since timestamp; Percona warns monthly or end-of-day reporting indexes can be missed by short windows. — https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-unused-indexes/ · keywords: $indexStats, index, Index Analysis with $indexStats and Unused-Index Detection

- [passage] Views are the result of aggregation pipelines. When you use $sample on a view, MongoDB appends the stage to the end of the view's aggregation pipeline syntax. Therefore, the $sample stage on a view is never the first stage and always results in a collection scan. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample/ · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/sample.md

- [passage] Because $queryStats reports only the operations that MongoDB samples, its output represents a subset of the operations run against your deployment. Counts and execution times reflect only the sampled operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] When an HMAC key is specified to the transformIdentifiers option, $queryStats uses the HMAC key to apply an HMAC-SHA-256 hash function on the following data: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] In sharded clusters, MongoDB records query statistics separately on each mongod and mongos when $queryStats is enabled. Shard servers also record statistics for queries that originate from mongos. These provide more complete shard-level metrics for queries that users route through mongos. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] When Atlas runs $queryStats on your deployment, it uses a unique HMAC key per Atlas organization to transform your data and avoid collecting sensitive information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [passage] Because the database profiler writes data to the [`system.profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/system-collections.md#mongodb-data--database-.system.profile) collection in a database, the profiler profiles some write activity, even for databases that are otherwise read-only. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, system.profile
- [passage] When using [Queryable Encryption](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption.md#std-label-qe-manual-feature-qe), CRUD operations against encrypted collections are omitted from the [`system.profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/system-collections.md#mongodb-data--database-.system.profile) collection. For details, see [Redaction.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/limitations.md#std-label-qe-redaction) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, system.profile · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md
- [passage] Number of times the operation had to wait for the [`acquireCount`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.locks.acquireCount) lock acquisitions because the locks were held in a conflicting mode. [`acquireWaitCount`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.locks.acquireWaitCount) is less than or equal to [`acquireCount`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.locks.acquireCount) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#output-fields · keywords: database profiler, acquireCount, acquireWaitCount
- [passage] When MongoDB writes query profile information to the log, the [`responseLength`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.responseLength) value is in a field named `reslen`. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#output-fields · keywords: database profiler, responseLength, reslen
- [passage] The following examples show the differences in log messages when `$queryStats` output is included. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/toggle-logging.md#examples · keywords: query shape, $queryStats
- [passage] The Query Profiler samples operations by using a bucketing algorithm that adjusts the sample size based on the width of the selected time range. Because of differences in bucket size, a wider time range might display fewer sampled operations than a narrower time range. For exact, unsampled operation counts, download your `mongod` logs. To learn more, see [View and Download MongoDB Logs.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-logs.md#std-label-mongodb-logs) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#data-display-limitations · keywords: database profiler, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] mongos performs a broadcast operation for queries that do not include the shard key, routing queries to all shards in the cluster. Some queries that do include the shard key may still result in a broadcast operation depending on the distribution of data in the cluster and the selectivity of the query. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router/ · keywords: index effectiveness · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharded-cluster-query-router.md

## How-to and procedures

- [passage] To view query performance in the Query Profiler, you must have [`Project Read Only`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Read-Only) or [`Project Observability Viewer`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Observability-Viewer) access to the project. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#required-access · keywords: database profiler, query optimization, Project Read Only, Project Observability Viewer
- [passage] To view query performance in the Query Profiler, you must have Project Read Only or Project Observability Viewer access to the project. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query optimization
- [passage] To change the other index options, drop the existing index with [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) before running [`db.collection.createIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.createIndexes) with the new options. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndexes.md#non-collation-and-non-hidden-options · keywords: $indexStats, index, db.collection.dropIndex(), db.collection.createIndexes() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.createIndex.md
- [passage] To drop an index, insert the index name and run [db.collection.dropIndex().](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#std-label-collection-drop-index) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/index-wildcard/index-wildcard-compound.md#use-a-helper-method-to-create-a-wildcard-index · keywords: $indexStats, index
- [passage] To establish recommended indexes, the Performance Advisor uses these metrics in a formula to calculate the Impact, or performance improvement that creating an index matching that query shape would cause. When the Performance Advisor suggests indexes, it ranks the indexes by their Impact. The Impact is determined by the total wasted bytes read. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking.md#how-performance-advisor-suggests-and-ranks-indexes · keywords: index, query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/index-ranking/
- [passage] Use the dropIndexes command or its shell helpers dropIndex() or dropIndexes() to terminate an in-progress index build. See Stop In-Progress Index Builds for more information. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation/ · keywords: $indexStats, index
- [passage] To get the index name or the index specification document for the [`db.collection.dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) method, use the [`db.collection.getIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.getindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.getIndexes) method. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropIndex.md#definition · keywords: $indexStats, index, db.collection.dropIndex(), db.collection.getIndexes()
- [passage] To drop a specific index, use the [`dropIndex()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindex.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndex) method and specify the index name: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/drop-index.md#drop-a-single-index · keywords: $indexStats, index, dropIndex()
- [passage] To drop multiple indexes, use the [`dropIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndexes) method and specify an array of index names: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/drop-index.md#drop-multiple-indexes · keywords: $indexStats, index, dropIndexes()
- [passage] To drop all indexes except the `_id` index, use the [`dropIndexes()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.dropindexes.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.dropIndexes) method: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/drop-index.md#drop-all-indexes-except-the-id-index · keywords: $indexStats, index, _id, dropIndexes()
- [passage] To sort by a metric in descending or ascending order, click the sort icon next to the associated column name once or twice, respectively. To sort by multiple columns, press Shift and click the sort icons in the order in which you want to multi-sort the table. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#select-query-shapes-to-chart · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To learn more about the command syntax and parameters, see the Atlas CLI documentation for [atlas performanceAdvisor slowQueryLogs list.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-performanceAdvisor-slowQueryLogs-list/) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor.md#view-slow-query-logs · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] Use this endpoint to reject a query shape (preventing it from executing on the cluster) or to unreject a previously rejected query shape (allowing it to execute again). This operation is idempotent: rejecting an already rejected query shape or unrejecting an already unrejected query shape will return 200 OK. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-queryShapeInsights-updateClusterQueryShape.md · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To view more details about a query shape, click on the row for the query shape to open the Query Shape Details view. This view contains the full query shape and query shape hash, each table metric listed above, and the following additional metrics: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#view-metrics-in-charts-and-tables · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/
- [passage] To view the current profiling level, see [`db.getProfilingStatus()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.getprofilingstatus.md#mongodb-method-db.getProfilingStatus) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#unset-a-filter · keywords: database profiler, db.getProfilingStatus() · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md
- [passage] To clear a profile filter, run `db.setProfilingLevel()` with the `filter: "unset"` option. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md#unset-a-filter · keywords: database profiler, db.setProfilingLevel(), filter: "unset"
- [passage] To block a query shape, use an operation rejection filter. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/query-shapes/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To view metrics with Query Shape Insights, you must have Project Observability Viewer, Project Data Access Read Only, Project Data Access Read/Write, Project Data Access Admin, or Project Owner access to the project. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To run $queryStats without the transformIdentifiers option, the user must have the queryStatsRead privilege action. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To run $queryStats with the transformIdentifiers option, the user must have the both the queryStatsRead and queryStatsReadTransformed privilege actions. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To learn how to control $queryStats logging behavior, see Toggle $queryStats Log Output. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape
- [passage] To use the MongoDB Node.js driver to add a $queryStats stage to an aggregation pipeline, use the $queryStats operator in a pipeline object. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/indexStats/
- [passage] To learn how to control `$queryStats` logging behavior, see [Toggle $queryStats Log Output.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/querystats/toggle-logging.md#std-label-queryStats-toggle-logging) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md#querystats-log-entries · keywords: query shape, $queryStats
- [passage] To enable or disable Performance Advisor and the Query Profiler for a project, you must have the [`Project Owner`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Project-Owner) role for the project or the [`Organization Owner`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/reference/user-roles.md#mongodb-authrole-Organization-Owner) role on its parent organization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#required-access · keywords: database profiler, Project Owner, Organization Owner
- [passage] To enable or disable Performance Advisor and the Query Profiler for a project, you must have the Project Owner role for the project or the Organization Owner role on its parent organization. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler

## Measurements and reference values

- [fact] The default slowms threshold is 100 ms and default sampleRate is 1.0. slowms and sampleRate are global (all databases in the process); profiling level and filter are per database when set via db.setProfilingLevel() but process-wide when set on the command line or config file. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] Profiler output goes to system.profile, a capped collection per database with a default size of 1 MB (roughly several thousand documents). To resize it, disable profiling, drop it, recreate it with db.createCollection('system.profile', {capped:true, size:N}), then re-enable profiling. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] Sampling differs by version: Atlas on 8.x records up to 100 read queries/s per host and no writes; from MongoDB 9.0 $queryStats samples 1% of reads and writes by default (internalQueryStatsSampleRate, internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate, 0.0-1.0). Infrequent shapes may be missing and totals jump after an 8.x to 9.0 upgrade. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats
- [passage] - On clusters running MongoDB 9.0 or later, Atlas randomly samples 1% of read and write operations by default. Displayed metric values reflect only sampled operations, approximately 1% of total operations. Query shapes that run infrequently may not appear in the results. This method also collects write operations (`insert`, `update`, and `delete`), which appear in Query Shape Insights alongside read operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights.md#how-atlas-collects-query-shape-statistics · keywords: query shape, insert, update, delete · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/query-shape-insights/
- [passage] In MongoDB 9.0, the default value changes from `0` to `0.01`, which enables query stats collection for read operations at a default sampling rate of 1%. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#query-stats-parameters · keywords: query shape,  to 
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 9.0, $queryStats collects stats for a sample of 1% of read and write operations by default. To change the sampling rate, set the internalQueryStatsSampleRate parameter for read operations or the internalQueryStatsWriteCmdSampleRate parameter for write operations. Both parameters accept a value between 0.0 and 1.0. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats.md
- [fact] $queryStats stores entries in an in-memory virtual collection limited to 1% of system memory. Each entry is keyed by query shape plus client info, read concern and collection type, so one shape can produce several entries; keyHash identifies the entry and queryShapeHash groups entries by shape. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/queryStats/ · keywords: query shape, Query Shapes and Query Hash and $queryStats

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [fact] The slow operation threshold is shared by the profiler and the diagnostic log. With logLevel 0, slow operations are logged at a rate set by slowOpSampleRate; at higher log verbosity all operations are logged regardless of latency. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] Slow-query log fields have grown by version: queryFramework (6.2), cpuNanos on Linux (6.3), queues and queryShapeHash (8.0), spill metrics (8.1), originalQueryShapeHash, slow in-progress entries via slowOpInProgressThresholdMs and a deadline field (8.3), and queryKnobs (9.0). — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] Atlas dynamically adjusts its slow query threshold by default (used by Performance Advisor and Query Profiler); users can opt out to a fixed 100 ms and MongoDB advises against going lower. Free (M0) clusters have the managed threshold disabled and it cannot be enabled; clusters with MongoDB Search do not support it. Toggling needs Project Owner. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/performance-advisor/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [fact] Since MongoDB 5.0, changes to profiler level, slowms, sampleRate or filter are written to the log file. Secondaries also log oplog applications slower than the threshold; the profiler does not capture slow oplog entries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler, query shape, Slow Query Monitoring (profiler and slow-query log and planSummary)
- [passage] | Name | Type | Required | Description | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | --clusterName | string | true | Human-readable label that identifies the cluster. | | --envelope | envelope | false | Flag that indicates whether Application wraps the response in an envelope JSON object. Some API clients cannot access the HTTP response headers or status code. To remediate this, set envelope=true in the query. Endpoints that return a list of results use the results object as an envelope. Application adds the status parameter to the response body. | | --groupId | string | true | Unique 24-hexadecimal digit string that identifies your project. Use the [/groups](#tag/Projects/operation/listProjects) endpoint to retrieve all projects to which the authenticated user has access. **NOTE**: Groups and projects are synonymous terms. Your group id is the same as your project id. For existing groups, your group/project id remains the same. The resource and corresponding endpoints use the term groups. | | -h, --help | | false | help for getClusterQueryShape | | -o, --output | string | false | preferred api format, can be ["json", go-template] This value defaults to "json". | | --outputFile | string | false | file to write the api output to. This flag is required when the output of an endpoint is binary (ex: gzip) and the command is not piped (ex: atlas command > out.zip) | | --pretty | | false | Flag that indicates whether the response body should be in the prettyprint format. | | --queryShapeHash | $queryStats | true | A SHA256 hash of a query shape, output by MongoDB commands like $queryStats and `$explain` or slow query logs. | | --version | string | false | API version to use when calling the Atlas API endpoints [options: "2025-03-12"]. If not set by the user, defaults to the latest version or the profile's api_version config value if set. This value defaults to "2025-03-12". | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-queryShapeInsights-getClusterQueryShape.md#options · keywords: database profiler, query shape, $explain · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-queryShapeInsights-updateClusterQueryShape.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-queryShapeInsights-getQueryShapeDetails.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/cli/current/command/atlas-api-queryShapeInsights-listClusterQueryShapes.md
- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `createIndexes` | string | The collection for which to create indexes. | | `indexes` | array | Specifies the indexes to create. Each document in the array specifies a separate index. | | `writeConcern` | document | Optional. A document expressing the [write concern](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/write-concern.md). Omit to use the default write concern. | | `commitQuorum` | integer or string | Optional. The minimum number of data-bearing replica set members (i.e. commit quorum), including the primary, that must report a successful [index build](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-replicated-build) before the primary marks the `indexes` as ready. You can resume some [interrupted index builds](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#std-label-index-operations-build-failure) when the commit quorum is set to the default `"votingMembers"`. See [`setIndexCommitQuorum`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/setindexcommitquorum.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.setIndexCommitQuorum) Replica set nodes in a commit quorum must have [`members[n].buildIndexes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.buildIndexes) set to `true`. If any voting nodes have `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `false`, you can't use the default `"votingMembers"` commit quorum. Either configure all nodes with `members[n].buildIndexes` set to `true`, or select a different commit quorum. Supports the following values: `"votingMembers"` - all data-bearing voting replica set members (*Default*). A "voting" member is any replica set member where [`members[n].votes`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/replica-configuration.md#mongodb-rsconf-rsconf.members-n-.votes) is greater than `0`.; `"majority"` - a simple majority of data-bearing replica set members.; `<int>` - a specific number of data-bearing replica set members.; A replica set [tag name.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/configure-replica-set-tag-sets.md) | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. Once set, this comment appears alongside records of this command in the following locations: [mongod log messages](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-messages-ref), in the `attr.command.cursor.comment` field.; [Database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#mongodb-data-system.profile.command) field.; [`currentOp`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.currentOp) output, in the [`command.comment`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/currentop.md#mongodb-data-currentOp.command) field. A comment can be any valid [BSON type](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/bson-types.md#std-label-bson-types) (string, integer, object, array, etc). | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/createIndexes.md#command-fields · keywords: $currentOp, database profiler, index, createIndexes, indexes, writeConcern

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `getMore` | long | The cursor identifier. | | `collection` | string | The name of the collection over which the cursor is operating. | | `batchSize` | positive integer | Optional. If `batchSize` is set, `getMore` returns the lesser of `batchSize` documents or 16 MiB. | | `maxTimeMS` | non-negative integer | Optional. Specifies how long the server waits for new documents matching a [tailable cursor](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/tailable-cursors.md#std-label-tailable-cursors-landing-page) query on a [capped collection](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/capped-collections.md#std-label-manual-capped-collection). `maxTimeMS` on a `getMore` for a tailable `awaitData` cursor is equivalent to [`maxAwaitTimeMS()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxawaittimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxAwaitTimeMS) Drivers set this value only for tailable cursors on capped collections where `awaitData` is `true`. Otherwise, the command that creates the cursor sets `maxTimeMS` as the cumulative time limit for the initial operation and all subsequent `getMore` operations. For tailable cursors with `awaitData` set to `true`, the following is true: If no value is provided, the wait time defaults to `1` (1000 milliseconds).; `maxTimeMS` on `getMore` specifies the maximum amount of time MongoDB waits for new documents to be inserted into the capped collection for that specific `getMore` command.; `maxTimeMS` is set individually by the driver for each call to `getMore`. MongoDB terminates operations that exceed their time limit using the same mechanism as [`db.killOp()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.killop.md#mongodb-method-db.killOp), but only at designated [interrupt points.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-interrupt-point) You cannot set `maxTimeMS` when calling `getMore` on a non-tailable cursor. Instead, set it using [`maxTimeMS()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.maxtimems.md#mongodb-method-cursor.maxTimeMS) when you create the cursor.; To use `getMore` with `maxTimeMS` on a tailable cursor, enable `awaitData` when you create the cursor using [`cursor.tailable()`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/cursor.tailable.md#mongodb-method-cursor.tailable); Setting `maxTimeMS` on the command that creates a cursor only sets the time limit for that operation. Use `getMore` to set a limit on further operations.; You can set or omit `maxTimeMS` for each call to `getMore`, and you don't have to use the same value.; For a tailable cursor, a timeout on `getMore` retains the documents accumulated before the timeout occurred in the cursor. For a non-tailable cursor, a timeout raises an error. | | `comment` | any | Optional. A user-provided comment to attach to this command. - [passage] If you restart the `mongod` as a standalone (that is, removing or commenting out [`replication.replSetName`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-replication.replSetName) or omitting [`--replSetName`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#std-option-mongod.--replSet)), the `mongod` cannot restart the index build. - [passage] | Stage | Description | | --- | --- | | Lock | The `mongod` obtains an exclusive `X` lock on the the collection being indexed. This blocks all read and write operations on the collection, including the application of any replicated write operations or metadata commands that target the collection. The `mongod` does not yield this lock. | | Initialization | The `mongod` creates three data structures at this initial state: The initial index metadata entry.; A temporary table ("side writes table") that stores keys generated from writes to the collection being indexed during the build process.; A temporary table ("constraint violation table") for all documents that may cause a key generation error. Key generation errors occur when a document has invalid keys for the indexed fields. For example, a document with duplicate field values when building a [unique index](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-unique.md#std-label-index-type-unique) *or* malformed [GeoJSON objects](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/geospatial-queries.md#std-label-geospatial-geojson) when building a [2dsphere index.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/indexes/index-types/geospatial/2dsphere.md#std-label-2dsphere-index) | | Lock | The `mongod` downgrades the exclusive `X` collection lock to an intent exclusive `IX` lock. The `mongod` periodically yields this lock to interleaving read and write operations. | | Scan Collection | For each document in the collection, the `mongod` generates a key for that document and dumps the key into an external sorter. If the `mongod` encounters a key generation error while generating a key during the collection scan, it stores that key in the constraint violation table for later processing. If the `mongod` encounters any other error while generating a key, the build fails with an error. Once the `mongod` completes the collection scan, it dumps the sorted keys into the index. | | Process Side Writes Table | The `mongod` drains the side write table using first-in-first-out priority. If the `mongod` encounters a key generation error while processing a key in the side write table, it stores that key in the constraint violation table for later processing. If the `mongod` encounters any other error while processing a key, the build fails with an error. For each document written to the collection during the build process, the `mongod` generates a key for that document and stores it in the side write table for later processing. The `mongod` uses a snapshot system to set a limit to the number of keys to process. | | Vote and Wait for Commit Quorum | A `mongod` that is *not* part of a replica set skips this stage. The `mongod` submits a "vote" to the primary to commit the index. Specifically, it writes the "vote" to an internal replicated collection on the [primary.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary) If the `mongod` is the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary), it waits until it has a commit quorum of votes (all voting data-bearing members by default) before continuing the index build process. If the `mongod` is a [secondary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary), it waits until it replicates either a "commitIndexBuild" or "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry: If the `mongod` replicates a "commitIndexBuild" oplog entry, it finishes draining the side writes table and moves to the next stage in the index build process.; If the `mongod` replicates an "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry, it aborts the index build and discards the build job. While waiting for commit quorum, the `mongod` adds any additional keys generated from write operations to the collection being indexed to the side writes table and periodically drains the table. | | Lock | The `mongod` upgrades the intent exclusive `IX` lock on the collection to a shared `S` lock. This blocks all write operations to the collection, including the application of any replicated write operations or metadata commands that target the collection. The `mongod` holds the `S` lock only while it drains the remaining records in the side writes table, and then releases it. | | Finish Processing Temporary Side Writes Table | The `mongod` continues draining remaining records in the side writes table. The `mongod` may pause replication during this stage. If the `mongod` encounters a key generation error while processing a key in the side write table, it stores that key in the constraint violation table for later processing. If the `mongod` encounters any other error while processing a key, the build fails with an error. | | Lock | After the `mongod` releases the `S` lock, it later acquires an exclusive `X` lock on the collection. This blocks all read and write operations on the collection, including the application of any replicated write operations or metadata commands that target the collection. The `mongod` does not yield this lock, but holds it only long enough to complete the final side writes drain, check constraint violations, and commit the index as ready. | | Drop Side Write Table | The `mongod` applies any remaining operations in the side writes table before dropping it. If the `mongod` encounters a key generation error while processing a key in the side write table, it stores that key in the constraint violation table for later processing. If the `mongod` encounters any other error while processing a key, the build fails with an error. At this point, the index includes all data written to the collection. | | Process Constraint Violation Table | If the `mongod` is the [primary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-primary), it drains the constraint violation table using first-in-first-out priority. If no keys in the constraint violation table produce a key generation error *or* if the table is empty, the `mongod` drops the table and creates a "commitIndexBuild" oplog entry. Secondaries can complete the associated index build after replicating the oplog entry.; If any key in the constraint violation table still produces a key generation error, the `mongod` aborts the build and throws an error. The `mongod` creates an associated "abortIndexBuild" oplog entry to indicate that secondaries should abort and discard the index build job. If the `mongod` is a [secondary](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/glossary.md#std-term-secondary), it drops the constraint violation table. Since the primary *must* successfully drain the constraint violation table prior to creating the "commitOplogEntry" oplog entry, the secondary can safely assume that no violations exist. | | Mark the Index as Ready | The `mongod` updates the index metadata to mark the index as ready for use. | | Lock | The `mongod` releases the `X` lock on the collection. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/index-creation.md#index-build-process · keywords: database profiler, index, mongod,  collection lock to an intent exclusive ,  lock. - [passage] Slow operations are logged based on `workingMillis`, which is the amount of time that MongoDB spends working on that operation. This means that factors such as waiting for locks and flow control do not affect whether an operation exceeds the slow operation threshold. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#profiler-options · keywords: database profiler, workingMillis
- [passage] When [`logLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.logLevel) is set to `0`, MongoDB records *slow* operations to the diagnostic log at a rate determined by [`slowOpSampleRate`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#profiler-options · keywords: database profiler, logLevel, slowOpSampleRate
- [passage] At higher `logLevel` settings, all operations appear in the diagnostic log regardless of their latency with the following exception: the logging of slow oplog entry messages by the secondaries. The secondaries log only the slow oplog entries; increasing the `logLevel` does not log all oplog entries. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#profiler-options · keywords: database profiler, logLevel
- [passage] The slow operation time threshold for an in-progress query, in milliseconds. MongoDB logs operations that run for longer than this threshold as slow in-progess queries. - [passage] Some high-latency [`$lookup`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/lookup.md#mongodb-pipeline-pipe.-lookup) operations may not generate a slow query log for the foreign collection. This can occur because slow query logs correspond with operations that are reported in the [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler), whereas latency metrics increment only when a [collection lock](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/faq/concurrency.md#std-label-faq-concurrency-locking) is acquired. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md#high-latency-lookup-operations · keywords: database profiler, $lookup · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/namespace-insights.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md
- [passage] If the `$lookup` query on a shard can perform a local read, the `$lookup` doesn't record a separate operation for querying the foreign collection. A local read refers to when the query on the foreign collection targets only the same shard where the current operation is being executed. As a result, the `$lookup` operation increases the `$collStats` latency metrics and operation counts, but does not generate a slow query log for the foreign collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/operator/aggregation/collStats.md#high-latency-lookup-operations · keywords: database profiler, $lookup, $collStats · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/namespace-insights.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] For a [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance, the command enables, disables, or configures the [database profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler.md#std-label-database-profiler). The profiler captures and records data on the performance of write operations, cursors, and database commands on a running [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instance. If the profiler is disabled, the command configures how slow operations are logged to the diagnostic log. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#definition · keywords: database profiler, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md

- [passage] | Field | Type | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `profile` | int | Configures the profiler level. The following profiler levels are available: `0`The profiler is off and does not collect any data. This is the default profiler level.`1`The profiler collects data for operations that exceed the `slowms` threshold or match a specified [filter.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-options-filter)When a filter is set:The `slowms` and `sampleRate` options are not used for profiling.; The profiler only captures operations that match the [filter.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setprofilinglevel.md#std-label-set-profiling-level-options-filter)`2`The profiler collects data for all operations.When set to level `2`, the profiler ignores user provided values for `slowms` and `filter`. Since profiling is not available on [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos), the [`profile`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#mongodb-dbcommand-dbcmd.profile) command cannot be used to set the profiling level to a value other than `0` on a [`mongos`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongos.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongos) instance. | | `slowms` | int | Optional. Default: 100 The slow operation time threshold, in milliseconds. Operations that run for longer than this threshold are considered *slow*. Slow operations are logged based on `workingMillis`, which is the amount of time that MongoDB spends working on that operation. This means that factors such as waiting for locks and flow control do not affect whether an operation exceeds the slow operation threshold. When [`logLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md#mongodb-parameter-param.logLevel) is set to `0`, MongoDB records *slow* operations to the diagnostic log at a rate determined by [`slowOpSampleRate`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) At higher `logLevel` settings, all operations appear in the diagnostic log regardless of their latency with the following exception: the logging of slow oplog entry messages by the secondaries. The secondaries log only the slow oplog entries; increasing the `logLevel` does not log all oplog entries. This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs`.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpThresholdMs) | | `sampleRate` | double | Optional. Default: 1.0 The fraction of *slow* operations that should be profiled or logged. `sampleRate` accepts values between 0 and 1, inclusive. This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.slowOpSampleRate) and does not affect the slow oplog entry log messages on secondaries. | | `filter` | object | Optional. A query that determines which operations are profiled or logged. The filter query takes the following form: `{ <field1>: <expression1>, ... }` The query can be any legal [`find()`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.collection.find.md#mongodb-method-db.collection.find) operation where the query `<field>` matches a field in the [profiler output.](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) This argument affects the same setting as the configuration option [`operationProfiling.filter`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/configuration-options.md#mongodb-setting-operationProfiling.filter). When `filter` is set, the `slowms` and `sampleRate` options are not used for profiling and slow-query log lines. | — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/command/profile.md#command-fields · keywords: database profiler, profile, The profiler collects data for operations that exceed the , slowms, sampleRate, , the profiler ignores user provided values for  · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md

- [passage] Slow operation log messages and database profiler entries include a cpuNanos field that specifies the total CPU time spent by a query operation in nanoseconds. The cpuNanos field is only available on Linux systems. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] The totalOplogSlotDurationMicros in the slow query log message shows the time between a write operation getting a commit timestamp to commit the storage engine writes and actually committing. mongod supports parallel writes. However, it commits write operations with commit timestamps in any order. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] MongoDB 8.3 also introduces slow in-progress query log entries. Queries trigger a slow-in progress log during execution. These logs contain less information than standard slow query logs. MongoDB logs queries at most once if the query's duration surpasses the operationProfiling.slowOpInProgressThresholdMs. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] When an operation specifies a time limit for a query, slow query logs contain a deadline field. deadline indicates the time the operation must complete by, which is equal to the time at the start of the operation plus the value of the query timeout. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] Starting in MongoDB 5.0, log messages for slow queries include a system.profile.authorization section. These metrics help determine if a request is delayed because of contention for the user authorization cache. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages/ · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md
- [passage] The [profiler entries](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/manage-the-database-profiler.md#std-label-database-profiler) and the [diagnostic log messages (i.e. mongod/mongos logmessages)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-message-slow-ops) for read/write operations include: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#logging-slow-operations · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] The CRUD operations below are omitted from the [slow operations](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/log-messages.md#std-label-log-message-slow-ops) query log and the [Database Profiler](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/database-profiler.md#std-label-profiler) `system.profile` collection when you run them on an encrypted collection. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/queryable-encryption/reference/limitations.md#query-log-and-database-profiler-redaction · keywords: database profiler, system.profile
- [passage] The Query Profiler diagnoses and monitors performance issues. This monitoring can expose slow-running queries and their key performance statistics in the Atlas UI. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] Atlas collects and displays statistics from any of your [`mongod`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/program/mongod.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongod) instances. The Query Profiler stores your `mongod` query [log data](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/mongodb-logs.md#std-label-mongodb-logs), which can be accessed directly through the Query Profiler or through the Atlas CLI, and use it to identify slow queries. Atlas displays this data on the Query Insights page, in the Query Profiler tab of an instance. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, mongod · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] The Atlas Query Profiler shows operations across your entire cluster by default. You can filter the Query Profiler view to only operations coming from specified hosts with the Filter by Hosts dropdown, which allows you to view data related to one or more specific hosts or to view primary or secondary host groups. The Query Insights option in the Cluster sidebar displays information to reveal slow database operations over a set time frame, such as the following: — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] Atlas manages the threshold for slow operations for each `mongod` host based on average operation execution time on that host. This threshold can be changed using the [`db.setProfilingLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md#mongodb-method-db.setProfilingLevel) [`mongosh`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/mongodb-shell.md#mongodb-binary-bin.mongosh) command. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, mongod, db.setProfilingLevel, mongosh · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] Changing the threshold for slow operations using [`db.setProfilingLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md#mongodb-method-db.setProfilingLevel) can impact performance and system log settings. Carefully consider any performance and security implications before you use [`db.setProfilingLevel`](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/method/db.setProfilingLevel.md#mongodb-method-db.setProfilingLevel) to adjust the Query Profiler settings on a production deployment. Query Profiler settings reset to default values following a node restart. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md · keywords: database profiler, db.setProfilingLevel
- [passage] The following section describes how to find slow queries using the Query Profiler. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/
- [passage] The Query Profiler uses a scatterplot chart and a table directly below the chart to help you find slow operations. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler.md#find-slow-queries-with-the-query-profiler · keywords: database profiler · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/

Query Profiler settings reset to default values following a node restart. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler
- [passage] Some high-latency $lookup operations don't generate a slow query log for the foreign collection. This can occur because slow query logs correspond with operations that are reported in the Query Profiler, whereas latency metrics increment only when a collection lock is acquired. — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/tutorial/query-profiler/ · keywords: database profiler
